segments.text: Promise.prototype.then()
segments.inlineMarkup: Promise.prototype.then()

segments.text: The then() method of Promise instances takes up to two arguments: callback functions for the fulfilled and rejected cases of the Promise. It stores the callbacks within the promise it is called on and immediately returns another Promise object, allowing you to chain calls to other promise methods.
segments.inlineMarkup: The *`then()`* method of [link]`Promise`[/link] instances takes up to two arguments: callback functions for the fulfilled and rejected cases of the `Promise`. It stores the callbacks within the promise it is called on and immediately returns another [link]`Promise`[/link] object, allowing you to [link]chain[/link] calls to other promise methods.

segments.text: Description
segments.inlineMarkup: [link]Description[/link]

segments.text: The then() method schedules callback functions for the eventual completion of a Promise — either fulfillment or rejection. It is the primitive method of promises: the thenable protocol expects all promise-like objects to expose a then() method, and the catch() and finally() methods both work by invoking the object's then() method.
segments.inlineMarkup: The `then()` method schedules callback functions for the eventual completion of a Promise — either fulfillment or rejection. It is the primitive method of promises: the [link]thenable[/link] protocol expects all promise-like objects to expose a `then()` method, and the [link]`catch()`[/link] and [link]`finally()`[/link] methods both work by invoking the object's `then()` method.

segments.text: For more information about the onRejected handler, see the catch() reference.
segments.inlineMarkup: For more information about the `onRejected` handler, see the [link]`catch()`[/link] reference.

segments.text: then() returns a new promise object but mutates the promise object it's called on, appending the handlers to an internal list if the promise is pending. segments.text: If you call the then() method twice on the same promise object (instead of chaining), then this promise object will have two pairs of settlement handlers. All handlers attached to the same promise object are always called in the order they were added. Moreover, the two promises returned by each call of then() start separate chains and do not wait for each other's settlement.

All handlers attached to the same promise object are always called in the order they were added. Moreover, the two promises returned by each call of `then()` start separate chains and do not wait for each other's settlement.

segments.text: Thenable objects that arise along the then() chain are always resolved — the onFulfilled handler never receives a thenable object, and any thenable returned by either handler are always resolved before being passed to the next handler. This is because when constructing the new promise, the resolve and reject functions passed by the executor are saved, and when the current promise settles, the respective function will be called with the fulfillment value or rejection reason. The resolving logic comes from the resolve function passed by the Promise() constructor.

This is because when constructing the new promise, the `resolve` and `reject` functions passed by the `executor` are saved, and when the current promise settles, the respective function will be called with the fulfillment value or rejection reason. The resolving logic comes from the `resolve` function passed by the [link]`Promise()`[/link] constructor.

segments.text: then() supports subclassing, which means it can be called on instances of subclasses of Promise, and the result will be a promise of the subclass type. You can customize the type of the return value through the [Symbol.species] property.

segments.text: The value returned from then() is resolved in the same way as Promise.resolve(). This means thenable objects are supported, and if the return value is not a promise, it's implicitly wrapped in a Promise and then resolved.

segments.text: A then call returns a promise that eventually rejects if the function throws an error or returns a rejected Promise.

segments.text: In all other cases, the returned promise eventually fulfills. In the following example, the first then() returns 42 wrapped in a fulfilled Promise, even though the previous Promise in the chain was rejected.
segments.inlineMarkup: In all other cases, the returned promise eventually fulfills. In the following example, the first `then()` returns `42` wrapped in a fulfilled Promise, even though the previous Promise in the chain was rejected.

segments.text:
Promise.reject(new Error("Oh no!"))
  .then(
    () => 99,
    () => 42,
  ) // onRejected returns 42 which is wrapped in a fulfilled Promise
  .then((solution) => console.log(`Resolved with ${solution}`)); // Fulfilled with 42
